subject: Marketplace billing handback & seller certification: next steps
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: aws_pm@amazon.com, jane.smith@acme.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace billing handback & seller certification: next steps

Hi team,

Quick note to align on the two parallel tracks AWS has flagged for the Acme Analytics listing: seller certification and the billing handback (the "usage handback") flow that ties Acme's SaaS metering to AWS fulfillment. AWS PM copied here listed a few gaps in our previous submission.

What I think we need to close in the next 10 business days:
- Seller certification owner + submission checklist (SOC2 + seller profile items)
- Finalized mapping between Acme's internal usage events and the AWS metering SKU identifiers (sample payload mapping attached)
- DocuSign SOW draft for procurement that includes a fallback for disputed usage claims

I attached a short spec (billing-spec-v2.pdf) with our proposed mapping and a proposed SLA handback window. Dev — can you confirm the webhook payload and whether the KV cache affects event timestamps? Acme — cc'd — we'll need a contact for procurement to confirm contract language.

Next steps:
1) Dev to confirm webhook schema and timestamp preservation by EOD Wed (Mar 21).
2) Hannah to confirm go/no-go timeline for seller certification submission by end of week.
3) Karthik to coordinate DocuSign SOW with Acme procurement once mapping and technical acceptance are agreed.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: jane.smith@acme.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: aws_pm@amazon.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace billing handback & seller certification: next steps

Thanks for the clear list, Karthik.

A few quick points from Acme procurement side:
- We need to see a sample DocuSign with explicit language on how disputed meter counts are handled and timeline for resolution (our standard is 45 days).
- The buyer team wants to understand how partial failures are surfaced (e.g., if webhook retries exceed window, what does the AWS entitlement record look like?).
- For seller certification: we have legal resources who need the seller profile + SOC2 attestation PDF.

I can loop in our procurement lead (procurement@acme.com) if you want formal redlines. For the technical mapping, please include an example of a high-volume burst scenario so our finance folks can validate monthly billing delta.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we are aiming to close procurement in the next three weeks.

Best,
Jane Smith
Head of Cloud Ops | Acme Analytics

From: dev_patel@redwood.com

Cc: aws_pm@amazon.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace billing handback & seller certification: next steps

Thanks — diving in on the technical bits. I looked at billing-spec-v2.pdf and sketched a minimal webhook + reconciliation approach. Attachment: webhook-schema.json (stub).

Summary of technical approach:
- Metering events: Acme will POST usage events to our endpoint with fields: timestamp_utc, customer_id, sku_id, unit_count, event_id. We will translate to AWS usage records using the sku_id -> AWS SKU mapping.
- Retry semantics: we keep a durable queue for inbound events and retry delivery to AWS for 7 days; after 7 days events are marked as "stale" and visible in the reconciliation interface.
- KV cache impact: KV caches only affect inference-hotline tokenization; they do not rewrite event timestamps. Timestamps are recorded at receipt (server_time) and preserved in the outbound AWS handback payload.
- Burst/aggregation: for high-volume bursts we will aggregate events into 1-minute buckets and emit aggregated units with an array of contributing event_ids to allow downstream dispute resolution.

Open items for Acme/procurement:
- Confirm whether 1-minute aggregation granularity is acceptable for billing accuracy.
- Confirm the dispute window (we default to 30 days in the platform, but Acme asked for 45 — we can support with SLA language).

Proposed acceptance criteria for go-live (staging -> prod):
1) End-to-end test with sample payloads (we'll provide a Postman collection).
2) Canary run against a subset of customers (5% traffic) for 3 days with reconciler alerts.
3) Contract signed with dispute window language and a simple escalation path to our CS team.

I can turn the stub into a full JSON schema by tomorrow.

- Dev Patel
Senior Backend Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — good progress. Quick decisions from my side:

1) Seller certification: Karthik, please own the seller profile submission. Targeting submission by next Tue (Mar 26). Karthik — confirm you have the SOC2 PDF and seller profile fields; if not, escalate to me by EOD Wed.

2) Procurement / DocuSign: I will share a procurement SOW draft (procurement-sow-draft.docx) with explicit dispute window options (30/45/60 days) so Acme procurement can pick. Jane — if you can loop in the procurement lead, we’ll aim to capture redlines in one pass.

3) Technical acceptance & canary: Dev — agree on the 1-minute aggregation option as long as we include per-event_ids metadata. Plan: run a 3-day 5% canary on staging, then promote. AWS PM — please confirm acceptance criteria for handback payloads (we need confirmation that server_time and aggregation arrays are acceptable).

I’ll summarize action items in a shared Google doc and set a weekly 30-minute sync for the next two weeks. Thanks — rapid tempo will get this over the line.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Marketplace & GTM | Redwood Inference
